clue.text: Doctors care? Lie put about in hypocritical show of concern

indicators.note: to put something about is to turn it round, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor's sympathy is exposed as a fake, a lie spread in a hollow show of feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is just letters; 'put about' rearranges DOCTORS CARE LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tears shed falsely, as a crocodile was fabled to weep over its prey, are a standard idiom for feigned sorrow.

clue.text: Catching someone in the net?

parts.note: reads like a fisherman or a goalkeeper, but the net is the internet and the catch is a romantic partner found through a matching service

explanation.surface: Someone is caught in a net, as by a fisherman or a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchmaking by machine or website is a way of landing a partner online, the net being the internet.

clue.text: Danish scientist shows strength in the field

definitions.meaning: Hans Christian ..., the Danish physicist who discovered electromagnetism
the old unit of magnetic field strength, named after him

explanation.surface: A Danish scientist demonstrates his power out in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the field' suggests fieldwork or sport, but it means a magnetic field.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist gave his surname to the CGS unit measuring magnetic field intensity.

clue.text: Alternatively, it could make one the worse …

indicators.note: says these letters could be made into a different word by rearranging them

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: One option might just leave a person worse off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the answer itself: its letters rearranged give I (one) plus THE WORSE, so 'could make' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words introduce a different possibility, so they are synonyms as sentence adverbs.

clue.text: … as it gets chums in a mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the preceding letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: so it goes when friends find themselves in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 3 down, but the clue stands alone: 'gets' is a link and 'mess' scrambles CHUMS IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is nearly always followed by 'as', and the pair means since or to the extent that, so it stands for a conjunction.

clue.text: Necessitate volunteers being included in line-up

indicators.note: the volunteers are put inside the other piece
in a down clue, up means the word line is written bottom to top

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Joining up demands that volunteers take their place in the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line-up' reads as a parade of volunteers, but it splits: 'up' turns line to ENIL in this down clue, and 'being included in' puts the volunteers inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to make it necessary as a consequence, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Stand, as soldiers may do at Leatherhead

parts.note: soldiers may stand at ease, so the thing they do here is ease

indicators.note: the head of the word Leather is its first letter

explanation.surface: Soldiers stand at ease in the Surrey town of Leatherhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Leatherhead is a town in Surrey; split it as 'Leather head' to take its first letter, L. 'at' is a link: soldiers stand at EASE.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's easel is a stand that holds a canvas or board upright.

clue.text: Sailors sought by TV producer

definitions.meaning: ordinary seamen in the Royal Navy, ranks below officer
viewing figures that a television producer hopes will be high

explanation.surface: A television producer goes looking for seamen to cast.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests casting sailors for a show; the second meaning is audience figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval ratings are non-commissioned sailors; TV ratings are audience measurements, two unrelated senses of one word.

clue.text: Auden permitted to compose impromptu

indicators.note: composing means putting together, so these letters are put together afresh

parts.note: the poet W. H. Auden, taken as written

explanation.surface: The poet Auden is allowed to write off the cuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compose' fits the poet, but it is the signal to rearrange AUDEN PERMITTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is done without planning, which is exactly what unplanned in advance means.

clue.text: Parade on All Fools' Day?

parts.note: All Fools' Day is the first of April, the day after the third month has gone by, so a parade then comes when that month is over

explanation.surface: A procession is held on April Fools' Day.
explanation.walkthrough: A military parade where troops file past; read the two words as the month of March being past, as it is by 1 April.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial parade in which troops file past a reviewing officer goes by this two-word name.

clue.text: Adversary's weekend article

parts.note: Sat, short for Saturday, is a day of the weekend

explanation.surface: An opponent writes a piece for the weekend paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is read as 'is', a link. The Devil's Hebrew name means adversary.
explanation.definitionFit: The name comes from the Hebrew for adversary or accuser, the Devil as opponent of God and man.

clue.text: Clubman doesn't begin to speak

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped from the start of the word

parts.note: one who putts on the green is a putter; also a golf club

explanation.surface: A member of a club cannot even start to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubman' suggests a member of a gentleman's club, but it is a golfer with his putter. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to say aloud or express in words, the same as to speak.

clue.text: Junky flagship?

definitions.meaning: a drug addict who injects straight into a vein
read as a chief vessel of a shipping line

explanation.surface: A junk boat leads the fleet as its flagship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junky' hints at a Chinese junk; it means an addict. The question mark flags the punning second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an intravenous drug user, and playfully the principal ocean liner of a fleet.

clue.text: Turn half left, then right in the gully — that's weird

indicators.note: turning round means the two letters are read in the opposite order
half of the four-letter word left is its first two letters
the right letter goes inside the gully

parts.note: a gully or channel is a ditch

explanation.surface: Directions for a walker: turn half left, then right into the gully, and things get strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reverses LE, the first half of 'left', to EL. 'that's' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means uncanny or supernatural, a close synonym of weird.

clue.text: Things not wanted on voyage

parts.note: echoes the luggage label for bags stowed in the hold, but means goods thrown overboard to lighten a ship

explanation.surface: Luggage labelled for the hold, not needed during the crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not wanted on voyage' was printed on labels for cabin trunks stowed below; here the things are literally unwanted and tossed into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo jettisoned from a ship in distress, which then washes up, is exactly goods the crew did not want aboard.

clue.text: Place most able to produce psychic phenomenon

indicators.note: these letters can produce a new word when they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A location best suited to make spirits appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'able to produce' rearranges PLACE MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritualists claim this substance exudes from a medium in a trance, a supposed psychic manifestation.

clue.text: Cu

parts.note: the chemical symbol for copper, but read as a word it is a three-letter verb lacking its final letter

explanation.surface: Just the chemical symbol for copper.
explanation.walkthrough: Cu looks like copper; read it as the word 'cut' with its tail removed, a curtailed cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The two letters are literally a truncated cut, and the phrase also means a quicker route.

clue.text: Artist rejected payment

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for payment is read backwards

parts.note: a reward is a payment for service

explanation.surface: A painter turns down the fee offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses REWARD.
explanation.definitionFit: One who draws pictures is a draughtsman or artist.

clue.text: Deadly sin of a soldier caught up in depravity

indicators.note: the soldier goes inside the word for depravity
in a down clue, up means the soldier is written bottom to top

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for a gunner or soldier

explanation.surface: One of the deadly sins: a soldier caught up in corrupt ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught up' turns the soldier into AR, written upwards in this down clue; 'in' puts it inside the depravity word, after the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed, under the name avarice, is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: The old banger's on the way from Norwich to Newmarket

definitions.text: on the way from Norwich to Newmarket

parts.note: the Model T Ford was an early mass-produced car; banger is British slang for an old car

explanation.surface: An old jalopy chugs along the road between two English towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Thetford is a Norfolk town on the road from Norwich to Newmarket. 's is read as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norfolk market town lies on the A11 between Norwich and Newmarket, so the location defines it.

clue.text: Overwhelm with paperwork

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone is swamped by forms and admin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paperwork' is split into two pieces, with work placed before paper; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to weigh down or crush, close to overwhelm.

clue.text: Highball contributes to alcohol in the bloodstream

indicators.note: the high ball is added into the middle of the drink

parts.note: a lob is a ball hit high into the air

explanation.surface: A whisky cocktail raises a drinker's blood alcohol level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highball' suggests a long drink, but it is a lob. The definition describes where the protein is found.
explanation.definitionFit: This protein is part of haemoglobin, found in red blood cells circulating in the blood.

clue.text: He works hard to avert rail disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things wrecked, so these letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A railwayman toils to prevent a train crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' rearranges AVERT RAIL; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful labour, so one who travails is a hard worker.

clue.text: Girl calling for someone to help

indicators.note: calling out a name means saying it, so the word is as heard

explanation.surface: A young woman calls out for assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the name Ida and the answer are pronounced the same. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An aider is one who aids, someone giving help.

clue.text: Fail to qualify and get the bird

definitions.meaning: pip is old slang for failing a candidate in an exam
a small songbird of the lark family

explanation.surface: Someone misses qualifying and is jeered off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get the bird' means be booed, but the bird is the definition. 'and get' links the two readings: pip it is a loose phrase for failing.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown songbird such as the meadow or tree variety.

clue.text: Diana could be a nymph

indicators.note: says the name could become another word if its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; Diana is also the Roman huntress goddess

explanation.surface: The goddess Diana might pass for a nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges DIANA.
explanation.definitionFit: A water nymph of Greek myth, presiding over springs and rivers.

clue.text: Church leaders are broke without capital

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the broke word goes round the rest

parts.note: the leading letters of Church, also its standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: The heads of the church have run out of money and have no funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without capital' reads as having no money, but capital is the definition. Bucharest is the capital of Romania.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital city of Romania.

clue.text: Women used a tear causing a royal response

indicators.note: causing means making, so these letters make something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: Women shedding a tear provoke a reaction from the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' rearranges WOMEN USED A TEAR. The answer is the remark attributed to Queen Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria is famously said to have used this phrase to rebuke a courtier's joke, a regal put-down.
